correctness.rationale: From \(J^{T}=-J\) and \(J^{T}J=I\), one gets \(J^2=-I\), \(\langle v,Jv\rangle=0\), and \(\|Jv\|=\|v\|\). Writing \(e=x-x_\star\) and \(s=L\gamma\), the extrapolated point is \(\hat e=(I-sJ)e\), \(F(\hat x)=L(J+sI)e\), and the Polyak projection coefficient is exactly \(\alpha=\gamma/(1+s^2)\). Hence \(e^+=(I-sJ)e/(1+s^2)\) and \(\|e^+\|^2=\|e\|^2/(1+s^2)\). The source critical-condition ratio is exactly \(s\), so admissibility is \(s\le A\). For bounded positive \(s_k\), the infinite product tends to zero exactly when \(\sum_k s_k^2=\infty\). The package exact-rational verifier independently reproduces the one-step identity and finite products in the canonical quarter-turn model.
risks: The theorem is intentionally restricted to skew isometries; general skew operators with unequal singular values are outside scope.

value.rationale: The exact skew-isometry family is a mathematically motivated stress test for rotational monotone problems. The equality identifies the sharp admissible step, the exact contraction factor, and a nontrivial variable-step convergence boundary \(\sum s_k^2=\infty\), which is more informative than a finite experiment or generic big-O bound.
risks: It remains a special structured family rather than a general operator theorem.

limitations: No claim is made for non-isometric skew operators or for stochastic PolyakEG.
